newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Audit Chamber slams Rosgosstrakh sale.
newsitem.headline: Russian Audit Chamber slams Rosgosstrakh sale.

text.p: Russia's Audit Chamber has found massive breaches of the law in the privatisation of Russia's biggest insurer OAO Rosgosstrakh and has sent materials to the Prosecutor-General's office, a Chamber official said on Tuesday.
Sergei Burkov, deputy head of inspection on control over state property, told Reuters the government had lost up to 198 billion roubles as a result of the violations.
"We are suggesting the State Property Committee's order on privatisating Rosgosstrakh should be cancelled," he said.
He said the Prosecutor-General's office was supposed by law to start its own investigation after receiving the Audit Chamber materials.
The Audit Chamber monitors public spending and property on behalf of parliament, and examined the Rosgosstrakh privatisation on the orders of the State Duma lower house.
Rosgosstrakh employees have bought 20 percent of the insurer's shares and a management team of nine people got a priority right to buy 30 percent at 10.52 roubles each.
The remaining 50 percent of shares are to be sold at a cash auction this year.
Burkov said the price of shares was calculated on assets without accumulation and social funds and for nine months of 1996, not the whole year.
Within the three months not taken into consideration the volume of assets grew sharply, Burkov said.
"So we are making a conclusion about significant losses," he said. "The deal should be cancelled."
As a big company, Rosgosstrakh should have been privatised under a special scheme, not under one of the schemes worked out by the government for smaller firms, he said.
Burkov said if the State Property Committee ignored the Audit Chamber conclusions, the chamber would insist that the Prosecutor-General's office conduct its own investigation.

Rosgosstrakh privatisation has already come under fire from a union of depositors in the company, which has filed a suit to the Moscow Arbitration Court against the State Property Committee ,fearing a privatised company would not repay money on policies issued before economic reforms started in 1992.
The court will consider the suit on June 2.

Burkov said the government had not received any dividends from its Rosgosstrakh shares since 1992, when it became a joint stock company, while its net profit over that period was over 77 billion roubles.
